key_insight: Cross-lingual transfer from Arabic and Persian can substantially improve biomedical translation for some low-resource Arabic-script languages, especially when using LoRA adapter merging or small supervised adaptation.
clinical_relevance: This could help expand access to biomedical information in under-resourced languages, but performance is uneven and may be insufficient for high-stakes clinical use.
method: Used Arabic and Persian as higher-resource pivot languages.
Fine-tuned small decoder-only LLMs with LoRA to create domain-specific pivot adapters.
Compared few-shot prompting, 500-sentence supervised adaptation, and zero-data adapter merging.
evidence_signal: On evaluation, supervised adaptation with 500 sentences reached CHrF++ 41.01 for Dari and 28.88 for Urdu, while adapter merging stayed within 3.5 CHrF++ of supervised Dari performance without extra target-language data.
watch_item: Pashto and Sorani Kurdish remained too weak for high-stakes deployment, showing that transfer may fail when language distance from the pivots is large.
paper_title: Biomedical Machine Translation for Low-Resource Arabic-Script Languages via Cross-Lingual Transfer and LoRA Adapter Merging
